A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Transformer learning study. All 13 pages of each version, including figures, equations, references and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer experiments on sinusoid regression and Omniglot classification, including predictability sweeps, learning trajectories and vocabulary-size manipulation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative learning-cost results in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The four-layer, four-head Transformer, task-specific inputs, jointly trained Omniglot ResNet, training losses and task-generation procedures remain unchanged. Prequential codelength is introduced as an analytical measure, not a model or training-method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use sinusoid regression and Omniglot binary classification, including the same vocabulary-size sweep. The added cost analysis uses predictability conditions already covered by the original parameter grids.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates additional baseline algorithms or competing architectures. The new cost analysis compares the existing ICL and IWL strategies; newly cited methods are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds a cumulative-loss evaluation over 50,000 steps, contrasting volatile environments with reliable cues against stable environments with unreliable cues. Equation 4 removes the denominator's stabilization term. Appendix A.1 relabels the sinusoid noise grid from sigma to sigma squared, consistent with the main-text variance definition; these changes do not establish rerunning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v1 supports its relative-cost explanation through qualitative reasoning and vocabulary-size manipulation. v2 adds a substantive quantitative test across both tasks using cumulative learning loss in Figure 5. The existing vocabulary-size analysis is retained as Figure 6, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 retains three random seeds per configuration, means and error bars representing plus or minus one SEM. The new cost figure follows this convention; no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: New Figure 5 supplies quantitative evidence central to the cost hypothesis: cumulative MSE is lower for IWL in sinusoid regression, while cumulative BCE is lower for ICL in Omniglot, under the respective strategy-favoring environments. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting performance improvements. Retained curves preserve their preference values, although Figure 4 slightly shifts the sinusoid trajectories' plotted training-step positions.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces a formal prequential-codelength definition, and Section 4.3 adds an unproved coupon-collector sample-complexity claim of Theta(KN log N). Section 3.4 also corrects the reversed interpretation of the preference score and removes its stabilization term. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The main predictability and bidirectional-transience claims remain. v2 refines the broad relative-computational-cost hypothesis into an explicit account combining environmental optimality with strategy-acquisition cost determined by task structure and inductive bias, emphasizing this account in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes potentially negligible ICL maintenance costs from difficult IWL acquisition and interprets cumulative loss as predicting initial strategy preference. It removes v1's explicit discussion of the limited predictability regimes represented by noise and AR(1) processes. The simplified-task and functional-versus-mechanistic limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproducibility statement promising public release of the complete codebase upon publication, but provides no access link establishing availability. Architecture, optimizer, training budget and compute disclosures remain, including 819 runs and approximately 410 TPU-hours.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the cost account's research positioning through minimum description length, simplicity bias and resource-rational analysis, including Blier and Ollivier and Lieder and Griffiths. Its introduction explicitly positions learning dynamics against the limitations of Wurgaft et al.'s rational-adaptation perspective. References associated with omitted biological examples and predictability-regime discussion are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, biological analogies, results and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. v2 shortens the title, moves model details after task descriptions, simplifies notation and adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements. It also introduces the contradictory heading 'Stable environments favor ICL' above text explaining that stability favors IWL.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel cost chart, resizes and relabels retained plots, rewrites captions and relocates figures within the conference template. The existing vocabulary plot becomes Figure 6. Figure 3's Omniglot caption changes its correct 'darker' description to 'lighter', moving a brightness inconsistency previously present in the prose into the caption.

improvement.justification: The new cost analysis and formal definition make the central relative-cost hypothesis more assessable, while Section 3.4 corrects v1's reversed score interpretation. These are limited net gains: costs are compared across different training environments, restricting causal interpretation, and v2 introduces a contradictory stability heading, retains a brightness-label inconsistency and removes a useful predictability-regime limitation.
